title: Target Hermitian Space for a Positive-Depth Block
body_html:
Target Hermitian Space for a Positive-Depth Block

Let \(\Gamma\in\mathbf g\) be the invertible semisimple element of a single positive-depth block. Among target \(\varepsilon'\)-hermitian \(D\)-modules \(V'\) with \(\dim_DV'=\dim_DV\), the condition \[ M^{-1}(\Gamma+\mathbf g_{x,r+})\ne\emptyset \] holds exactly for the isometry class of \(V_\Gamma\).
proof_html:
The definition of \(V_\Gamma\) gives one example: for the identity map \(w:V\to V_\Gamma\), the adjoint relation gives \(M(w)=\Gamma\).

Conversely, suppose \(V'\) satisfies the displayed condition. Positive-depth moment-map surjectivity supercuspidal_theta.positive_depth_moment_map_surjectivity lets us choose \(w\in\operatorname{Hom}_D(V,V')\) with \[ M(w)=\Gamma. \] Then for all \(v_1,v_2\in V\), \[ \langle wv_1,wv_2\rangle_{V'} = \langle v_1,\Gamma v_2\rangle_V = \langle v_1,v_2\rangle_{V_\Gamma}. \] Thus \(w\) is an isometry \(V_\Gamma\simeq V'\), proving uniqueness of the target hermitian space.
